maria_dev: Quick follow-up from the 'siloed quotas' RFC — we need to pick a contract for gateway <-> quota-service handshake. Two options I sketched: (A) strictly-consistent per-tenant counters at gateway (fast rejections, heavier invalidation) vs (B) optimistic local reservoir with periodic reconciliation. Pros/cons? I'm leaning to (B) + circuit-breaker on mismatch. Thoughts? cc @tomo @alyssa_platform


 tomo: I'm leaning optimistic too, as long as we bound local memory and drift. If every gateway keeps full counters we blow up state. Local reservoirs with caps + TTL are much cheaper.


 kevin_sre: Concern: optimistic lets bursts through that we might later revoke. That can mean user-visible work completed and business impact. Need clear revoke semantics and client-facing error codes (e.g., 429-revoked) so callers can handle.


 maria_dev: Agreed. Proposal: gateways mint `soft-token` leases up to `reserved_local_capacity` per-tenant. Each soft-token has `lease_id` + `issued_at` + `ttl`. Quota-service reconciles periodically and can return `revoke` for lease_ids. Gateways must attempt graceful cancellation where possible (streaming chunk cancel, backpressure) and return a special error if already completed.


 alyssa_platform: Implementation Q: streaming requests are tricky. We can't retroactively take back generated output. Maybe require streaming leases to be much shorter (eg 5s) and force checkpoints at chunk boundaries so we can stop issuing more chunks after a revoke. Also document best-practice in SDKs.


 tomo: Also recommend we compute a running divergence metric (KL-like) between observed tenant usage and baseline. If divergence exceeds threshold, gateway reduces soft-token cap immediately and flags tenant for probation. This helps detect coordinated abuse patterns that don't look like simple token spikes.


 kevin_sre: For abuse scoring, let's avoid heavy ML in the hot path. Use an ensemble of heuristics: EWMA of rps for burstiness, sequence-entropy drop (repeating prompts / low entropy), and rapid model-variant switching. Combine into a weighted score -> probation -> temporary hard-throttle. Keep weights configurable per-org.


 maria_dev: API sketch for gateway <-> quota-service: 1) `POST /lease` returns `[{lease_id, ttl, accepted}]` (sync). 2) `POST /reconcile` accepts batches `[{lease_id, tenant, consumed}]` and returns overdrawn list. 3) `POST /revoke` accepts `lease_id` proto for immediate revoke. TTL default 30s. Gateways can pass `expected_loss_rate` to tune optimism. Thoughts on shapes?


 infra-bot: deploy succeeded: quota-service v2 (lease endpoints) rolled to staging — @maria_dev


 alyssa_platform: Ops/observability: we must emit per-lease lifecycle traces (issued, consumed, reconciled, revoked) and tag with `origin-gw` so we can link user-facing 429s to revoked leases. Also expose `revoke_reason` (eg "abuse_score", "reconcile_overdraw").


 tomo: Cross-region failure case: if gateway loses connectivity to local quota-service region, fallback to remote region with reduced soft-token cap (e.g., 10% of normal) and escalate to incident if fallback lasts > 2m. SLOs should document this behaviour.


 kevin_sre: Reconcile semantics: must be idempotent and tolerate duplicate deliveries. `POST /reconcile` should accept `request_id` and honor last-write-wins for consumed totals. Also accept partial batches and respond with per-item status to allow gateway replay.


 maria_dev: Ownership question: who owns the `revoke` automation and runbooks? My take: platform team owns the gateway contract + SDK changes; SRE owns revoke runbooks, incident playbooks, and quota-service ops. Platform will implement changes and test harness; SRE will add dashboards and alerts.


 alyssa_platform: Platform will take gateway changes. SRE to own revoke runbooks + telemetry dashboards. I'll pair with @tomo for unit tests + simulation harness.


 tomo: I'll start a PR to add the `lease` client in gateway repo and a synthetic load harness that runs 10k tenants to validate no bulk overdraw patterns.


 maria_dev: Ok — I'll compose an RFC update with the above contract, include API shapes, revoke semantics, and a short simulation plan. If no objections I'll post by EOD and tag eng-infra + eng-platform. :thumbsup:


 kevin_sre: One more: add an unambiguous client error code for revoked leases (`429.REVOKED_LEASE`) and ensure SDKs surface it separately from regular 429 so product teams can make informed decisions.


 maria_dev: Good call. Adding that to the API section in the RFC. Thanks all.
